metadata.title: UX Research Insight Validator
metadata.persona: Bingjie Zhou (student narration; Kokoro is preview only)
metadata.bookend_exempt_reason: INFO 7375 student pitch: use a self-attributed hesitant-writer opener, not the toolkit host persona; no verdict card; own voice in final edit.
metadata.audience: UX researchers, UX hiring managers, and INFO 7375 reviewers

beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Bingjie Zhou. My project asks a simple question: when AI summarizes interviews, how can we verify its findings?
beats.motion_claim: The question is corrected from summary generation to verification.

qc.sparse_reason: Typed, corrected question is the action.

beats.narration_text: Three terms: a finding is a research claim, evidence is what participants actually said, and an audit checks whether the claim follows from that evidence.

terms.meaning: checking whether a claim follows from evidence

qc.sparse_reason: Brief definitions card.

beats.narration_text: AI can summarize user interviews in seconds. But a fluent summary is not necessarily a faithful one.

shot.visual_intent: A stack of fictional interview pages slides into a schematic AI box; a clean summary page comes out. Small label: CONSTRUCTED.
shot.motion_claim: A stack of fictional interview pages slides into a schematic AI box; a clean summary page comes out. Small label: CONSTRUCTED.

qc.sparse_reason: Show-tell intentionally uses one isometric drawing per beat with short labels. This does not waive contrast, empty-frame, or edge-bleed checks.

beats.narration_text: It might exaggerate one comment, overlook a disagreement, or turn a possibility into a fact. For UX research, those mistakes matter because research findings can shape real design decisions.

shot.visual_intent: One summary page incorrectly grows to cover two disagreeing quote cards, then an arrow carries it toward a design sketch. Labels: CLAIM, QUOTES.
shot.motion_claim: One summary page incorrectly grows to cover two disagreeing quote cards, then an arrow carries it toward a design sketch. Labels: CLAIM, QUOTES.

qc.sparse_reason: Show-tell intentionally uses one isometric drawing per beat with short labels. This does not waive contrast, empty-frame, or edge-bleed checks.

beats.narration_text: My proposed final project is UX Research Insight Validator: an AI-assisted workflow that checks research findings against their original interview evidence.

shot.visual_intent: One illustrated audit desk accepts a proposed finding and the original interview pages. Label: PROPOSED.

show.event: two source objects move into desk

shot.motion_claim: One illustrated audit desk accepts a proposed finding and the original interview pages. Label: PROPOSED.

beats.narration_text: I plan to build a small, reproducible Python-based workflow with structured outputs, sample reports, and tests. This is a proposal, not a working product yet.

shot.motion_claim: A proposed workflow grows from Python block to JSON report to test checklist; none is presented as running code. Label: PROPOSED.

beats.narration_text: Tools such as Dovetail and Looppanel already support AI-assisted research analysis, so generating themes alone would not be a meaningful difference.

shot.visual_intent: Two generic platform cards marked Dovetail and Looppanel are next to a stack of synthesized themes; neither card impersonates a real UI.
shot.motion_claim: Two generic platform cards marked Dovetail and Looppanel are next to a stack of synthesized themes; neither card impersonates a real UI.

qc.sparse_reason: Show-tell intentionally uses one isometric drawing per beat with short labels. This does not waive contrast, empty-frame, or edge-bleed checks.

beats.narration_text: My focus will be narrower: auditing individual claims for missing support, overgeneralization, and minority perspectives that a summary may overlook.

shot.visual_intent: One claim card moves through three visible inspection gates: EVIDENCE, SCOPE, VOICES. A small dissenting quote remains visible. Label: PROPOSED.
shot.motion_claim: One claim card moves through three visible inspection gates: EVIDENCE, SCOPE, VOICES. A small dissenting quote remains visible. Label: PROPOSED.

beats.narration_text: I will also connect questionable findings to possible design risks, rather than simply generating another polished summary.

shot.visual_intent: A warning dot appears on a disputed finding; a branching arrow points toward a possible design decision. Label: PROPOSED.
shot.motion_claim: A warning dot appears on a disputed finding; a branching arrow points toward a possible design decision. Label: PROPOSED.

beats.narration_text: The first runnable step will be simple: check whether a cited quotation actually appears in its source transcript, and return the source ID.

beats.narration_text: After that, I will add checks for distorted claims and overlooked perspectives, plus a short note on potential design impact.

beats.narration_text: Building reliable AI checks and systematic evaluations will be new learning for me. My goal is not to replace researchers, but to help them question AI-generated findings before those findings influence design.

beats.narration_text: Before trusting an AI research finding, ask three questions. Which exact quotes support it? Whose views might be missing? And what design decision could it influence?
